features: Native filesystem binding detects an explicit callback in its standard argument position. Callback-capable task constructors retain the old promise entry points and allocate no promise target in callback mode. Owner-thread result/error delivery invokes the callback directly in the real request scope, followed by actual cleanup.

Ordinary callback adapters, including vector reads/writes, now forward callbacks to the native lane with existing result shapes. Early abort callbacks queue through nextTick. Request scopes restore creation-time async-local state for both callback and promise requests, then restore the caller.

Node/Home controls validate callback read/write/stat/open/close/error, buffer identity, request identity and context. All 25 native groups and selected unchanged originals pass, including callback vector process checks and worker shutdown.
limitations: Compound rm/cp validation/walker adapters, directory and glob callback machinery, full request grouping/receiver parity, broader abort/exception/shutdown/collection and all-platform behavior remain open in #877. Windows UV callback paths are implemented but unverified.

Promise engine creation/resolve hooks and continuation IDs, sockets/DNS/worker producer integration and complete fs/async-hook parity remain open. Node optimized readFile may use an internal callback receiver; the initial stricter fixture expectation was corrected without changing upstream assertions.

Twenty original files retain 110 passes, twelve process checks, zero failures/skips/TODOs and 99 filtered cases. Exact ordinary fs filters validate. Earlier #874/#872 remain open and were not rerun. Original source hashes and assertions/snapshots are unchanged.

Pre-fix bounded failure, repeated disk guard stops/admission refusals, partial live browser cache cleanup and inactive compiler-cache reclamation are retained. Source/worktree/tmp evidence and active updater were preserved; guard thresholds and deadlines remain unchanged. Final-source recovered build passes 54/54.

Pickier retains three existing fs.ts prefer-const diagnostics and two warnings; committed baseline reproduces the three errors. This is not a clean whole-repository lint claim. Corpus #876, performance #869/#873, HTTPS #875/#532 and context #871/#856 remain open. Excluded constructor/Deno regressions were not rerun. Full Bun suite and Release/ASAN/all-platform verification remain open under #66.
